## 1. The Color Pipeline

The boxxy color pipeline transforms interaction entropy into deterministic,
perceptually-dispersed color streams across every rendering substrate.

**Seed derivation.** Terminal interactions (damage regions, keystrokes, cursor
moves) feed an `EntropyCollector` that hashes events via SHA-256 into a 64-bit
seed (per RFC 6943 §4). The seed is then scattered through the golden ratio
fractional part to maximize hue dispersion even for adjacent seed values.

**Golden angle spiral.** Each successive color advances by
$\varphi^{-2} \times 360° \approx 137.508°$ on the HCL hue wheel---the same
angle that maximizes packing in sunflower phyllotaxis. This is the `GoldenAnglePrecise`
constant (`137.5077640500378`). A secondary `PlasticAngle` ($\approx 205.14°$)
from the plastic constant $\rho$ ($x^3 = x + 1$) provides the ternary/3D analog.

**GF(3) tagging.** Every color in the stream carries a trit: index mod 3 maps to
`{Zero, One, Two}` = `{Coordinator(0), Generator(+1), Verifier(-1)}` in balanced
ternary. The `GF3Palette` assigns canonical RGBA values:

| GF(3) Elem | Balanced | Role | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | Coordinator | `#F59E0B` (amber) |
| 1 | +1 | Generator | `#A855F7` (purple) |
| 2 | -1 | Verifier | `#2E5FA3` (blue) |

**Flick timing.** Each color event is stamped with a `TritTick`---a flick
(1/705,600,000 s) tagged with a GF(3) element. Within each frame, a
`FrameTriad` places Plus at offset 0, Ergodic at 1/3, Minus at 2/3, ensuring
per-frame conservation: $1 + 0 + 2 \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$.

```{mermaid}

    B --> C["SplitMix64 / φ scatter<br/>baseHue ∈ [0,360)"]
    C --> D["Golden Angle Spiral<br/>hue += 137.508° per step"]
```

## 2. Platform Matrix

| Platform | Renderer | Color depth | Flick divisor | Trit encoding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| macOS (boxxy native) | Core Graphics / Metal | 30-bit HDR | All Hz integer | RGBA + trit byte |
| HaikuOS (boxxy haiku) | app_server / BView | 32-bit BGRA | All Hz integer | BGRATrit struct |
| Terminal (Ghostty) | ANSI SGR 24-bit | 24-bit RGB | 144Hz native | `ESC[38;2;r;g;b` + trit |
| Terminal (Kitty) | Kitty graphics protocol | 24-bit + alpha | 60Hz typical | Sixel or kitty PNG |
| EWW (Emacs) | HTML/CSS `rgb()` | 24-bit CSS | N/A (repaint) | `span.trit-plus/minus/zero` |
| Web (Quarto HTML) | CSS + Canvas | 32-bit RGBA | `requestAnimationFrame` | CSS custom property |

## 3. Haiku Color Rendering

HaikuOS provides a direct rendering path with no X11 or Wayland intermediary.
The `app_server` composites BView-drawn content through a
display-server-integrated pipeline---the same architecture that made BeOS
famous for media responsiveness.

### BView Color API

```cpp
// GF(3) palette mapped to BView high/low colors
void TritColorView::Draw(BRect updateRect) {
    // GF3Palette equivalents in Haiku's rgb_color
    static const rgb_color kCoordinator = {0xF5, 0x9E, 0x0B, 0xFF}; // amber
    static const rgb_color kGenerator   = {0xA8, 0x55, 0xF7, 0xFF}; // purple
    static const rgb_color kVerifier    = {0x2E, 0x5F, 0xA3, 0xFF}; // blue

    // SetHighColor for foreground trit glyph
    SetHighColor(kGenerator);
    // SetLowColor for background field
    SetLowColor(kCoordinator);

    FillRect(updateRect, B_SOLID_LOW);
    DrawString("⊕", BPoint(10, 20));  // trit +1 glyph
}
```

### Native BGRA32 Pixel Format

Haiku's `BBitmap` uses BGRA32 natively (B_RGBA32 = B, G, R, A byte order),
matching the app_server's internal compositing format. No swizzling needed.
The trit byte occupies a fifth channel in the boxxy `BGRATrit` struct:

```cpp
struct BGRATrit {
    uint8 blue;
    uint8 green;
    uint8 red;
    uint8 alpha;
    int8  trit;  // -1, 0, +1 (balanced ternary)
};
```

### BMessage-Based Trit-Tick Protocol

boxxy's Haiku VM (running under Apple Virtualization.framework on macOS)
communicates color updates via BMessage---Haiku's native IPC:

```cpp
// Sending a trit-tick color update
BMessage msg('TRIT');
msg.AddInt64("flick", when);           // flick timestamp
msg.AddInt8("trit", tritValue);        // -1, 0, +1
msg.AddInt32("rgb", (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b);
msg.AddFloat("hue", hue);             // golden angle position
messenger.SendMessage(&msg);
```

The Haiku tile runs as a `Verifier(-1)` in the cross-platform GF(3) balance,
providing a substrate-independent validation of color conservation.

## 4. Bandwidth Stack by Platform

Each platform imposes a different perception bandwidth ceiling. The pyramid
below computes bits-per-second of color information reaching the observer,
factoring in color depth, frame rate, and the GF(3) trit overhead.

```{ojs}
//| label: fig-bandwidth
//| fig-cap: "Perception Bandwidth Pyramid by Platform"

platforms = [
  { name: "macOS (Metal HDR)",    depth: 30, hz: 120, tritBits: 1.585,
    area: 3840*2160, fillFrac: 0.3 },
  { name: "HaikuOS (app_server)", depth: 32, hz: 60,  tritBits: 1.585,
    area: 1920*1080, fillFrac: 0.5 },
  { name: "Ghostty (SGR 24-bit)", depth: 24, hz: 144, tritBits: 1.585,
    area: 200*50,    fillFrac: 1.0 },
  { name: "Kitty (graphics)",     depth: 32, hz: 60,  tritBits: 1.585,
    area: 200*50,    fillFrac: 0.8 },
  { name: "EWW (CSS rgb)",        depth: 24, hz: 30,  tritBits: 1.585,
    area: 120*40,    fillFrac: 0.6 },
  { name: "Quarto (Canvas)",      depth: 32, hz: 60,  tritBits: 1.585,
    area: 800*600,   fillFrac: 0.4 }
]

bandwidth = platforms.map(p => ({
  ...p,
  bitsPerPixelPerFrame: p.depth + p.tritBits,
  pixelsPerFrame: p.area * p.fillFrac,
  get bps() { return this.bitsPerPixelPerFrame * this.pixelsPerFrame * p.hz; },
  get mbps() { return this.bps / 1e6; }
}))

Plot = import("https://esm.sh/@observablehq/plot@0.6")

Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 180,
  height: 300,
  x: { label: "Megabits per second", type: "log" },
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(bandwidth, {
      y: "name",
      x: "mbps",
      fill: d => d.name.includes("macOS") ? "#A855F7"
               : d.name.includes("Haiku") ? "#2E5FA3"
               : "#F59E0B",
      sort: { y: "x", reverse: true }
    }),
    Plot.text(bandwidth, {
      y: "name",
      x: "mbps",
      text: d => `${d.mbps.toFixed(1)} Mb/s`,
      dx: 5,
      textAnchor: "start"
    })
  ]
})
```

## 5. GF(3) Conservation Across Platforms

When boxxy tiles span multiple substrates simultaneously, the GF(3)
conservation law holds **across rendering backends**:

| Tile | Platform | Trit | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top-left | macOS (native) | +1 | Generator |
| Top-right | HaikuOS (VM) | -1 | Verifier |
| Bottom-left | Terminal (Ghostty) | 0 | Coordinator |
| Bottom-right | EWW (Emacs) | 0 | Coordinator |

$$\sum \text{trits} = (+1) + (-1) + 0 + 0 = 0 \quad \checkmark$$

This is precisely `gf3.IsBalanced([]gf3.Elem{One, Two, Zero, Zero})` returning
`true`---the same conservation law from `verified/GF3.dfy` now enforced across
physical rendering substrates.

The `FindBalancer` function from `gf3.go` generalizes this: given any three
platform trits, it computes the fourth tile's required role. If macOS is
Generator(+1), Ghostty is Coordinator(0), and EWW is Coordinator(0), then:

$$d = (3 - (1 + 0 + 0)) \bmod 3 = 2 \implies \text{Verifier}(-1)$$

Haiku **must** be the Verifier. The substrate is determined by the algebra.

## 6. Flick Arithmetic

A **flick** is $1/705{,}600{,}000$ of a second. The magic of this number:
$705{,}600{,}000 = 2^6 \times 3^2 \times 5^2 \times 7^2 \times 8 \times 25$,
or more precisely $2^9 \times 3^2 \times 5^5 \times 7^2$. Every standard frame
rate divides it evenly---no floating-point frame boundaries.

```{python}
#| label: fig-flick-divisors
#| fig-cap: "Flick divisors for standard frame rates"

FLICKS_PER_SECOND = 705_600_000

frame_rates = [24, 25, 30, 48, 50, 60, 90, 100, 120, 144]
rows = []
for hz in frame_rates:
    fpf = FLICKS_PER_SECOND // hz
    remainder = FLICKS_PER_SECOND % hz
    rows.append({"Hz": hz, "Flicks/frame": fpf, "Remainder": remainder,
                 "Frame ms": round(1000/hz, 4)})

import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(df.to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nAll remainders zero: {all(r['Remainder'] == 0 for r in rows)}")
```

```{ojs}
//| label: fig-divisibility-lattice
//| fig-cap: "Frame rate divisibility lattice"

rates = [24, 25, 30, 48, 50, 60, 90, 100, 120, 144]

// Build divisibility edges: a -> b if b % a == 0 and b != a
edges = []
for (const a of rates) {
  for (const b of rates) {
    if (b > a && b % a === 0) {
      // Check it's a direct divisor (no intermediate c with a|c|b)
      let direct = true
      for (const c of rates) {
        if (c > a && c < b && c % a === 0 && b % c === 0) {
          direct = false
          break
        }
      }
      if (direct) edges.push({ from: a, to: b })
    }
  }
}

// Assign y-position by "level" in lattice (number of divisors in set)
levelOf = (hz) => rates.filter(r => r < hz && hz % r === 0).length
nodes = rates.map(hz => ({
  hz,
  level: levelOf(hz),
  fpf: 705600000 / hz
}))

maxLevel = Math.max(...nodes.map(n => n.level))

// Simple force-directed-ish layout: x by hz, y by level
nodePos = Object.fromEntries(nodes.map((n, i) => [
  n.hz,
  { x: 50 + (i / (nodes.length - 1)) * 500, y: 250 - n.level * 55 }
]))

svg`<svg width="600" height="300" style="background:#1a1a2e;font-family:monospace">
  ${edges.map(e => {
    const p1 = nodePos[e.from], p2 = nodePos[e.to]
    return svg`<line x1="${p1.x}" y1="${p1.y}" x2="${p2.x}" y2="${p2.y}"
                     stroke="#F59E0B" stroke-width="1.5" opacity="0.6"/>`
  })}
  ${nodes.map(n => {
    const p = nodePos[n.hz]
    const fill = n.hz % 3 === 0 ? "#A855F7" : n.hz % 2 === 0 ? "#2E5FA3" : "#F59E0B"
    return svg`<g>
      <circle cx="${p.x}" cy="${p.y}" r="18" fill="${fill}" opacity="0.9"/>
      <text x="${p.x}" y="${p.y + 4}" text-anchor="middle"
            fill="white" font-size="11">${n.hz}</text>
    </g>`
  })}
  <text x="300" y="290" text-anchor="middle" fill="#888" font-size="10">
    705,600,000 = 2⁹ × 3² × 5⁵ × 7²  —  all Hz divide evenly
  </text>
</svg>`
```

### Trit-Tick Frame Triads

Within each frame, `FrameTriad` distributes three sub-frame trit-ticks at
offsets 0, 1/3, and 2/3 of the frame duration:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-triads
#| tbl-cap: "Sub-frame trit-tick positions for 60Hz and 144Hz"

FLICKS = 705_600_000
for hz in [60, 144]:
    fpf = FLICKS // hz
    third = fpf // 3
    print(f"\n{hz}Hz — {fpf:,} flicks/frame ({1000/hz:.3f} ms)")
    for i, (offset_frac, trit, role) in enumerate([
        (0, "+1", "Generator"), (1, " 0", "Coordinator"), (2, "-1", "Verifier")
    ]):
        offset = i * third
        print(f"  [{trit}] {role:12s} @ flick {offset:>10,}  ({offset/FLICKS*1000:.4f} ms)")
    print(f"  Sum: +1 + 0 + (-1) = 0  ✓")
```
